<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6f2bd4f84c98dcac81b0d745fcc16a35641ecc45` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Scope: skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-automation/references/examples-flows.md, skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md, skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/naming.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/validation.md, skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md, .github/workflows/lint.yml + packages/spec/scripts/check-skill-served-sections.ts, packages/spec/scripts/skill-served-sections.json, packages/spec/package.json (the `check:skill-served-sections` script line), packages/spec/scripts/check-generated.ts (the ledger row), scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs (the seven rows)
Security-touching: yes

Reviewed from: card #34771 (body and all five comments), PR #35131 (body, 16-file list, net diff against `main`, merge base `958ee03594`), the check-runs on the head. Read, not reviewed: the spec on `origin/main` (`b1eb500dc7`), and the hosted table and reader the card cites (`published-refs.ts`, `published-skills.ts`, cloud `aa67666`).

Check-runs on the head at 07:16Z: 60 `success`, 10 `skipped` (opt-in or schedule-only), 0 red, none pending (`Test Core (9/10)` was the last to conclude). Every gate that reads the reviewed files has concluded: `Type Check · source gates` is `success`, with its steps `Check the skill sections served to MCP clients keep their headings and valid JSON`, `Published skills token ratchet`, the skill docs / refs / links / compatibility checks and `Lane verdict` all `success`; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and the PR-body guards are `success`.

Why `Security-touching: yes`: three changed hunks teach permission or sharing behaviour. `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` rewrites the permission-set example (field read mask, `rollupSourceUnreadableReason`); `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` adds an object example with an authored `sharingModel` and deletes a sentence on what an omitted `sharingModel` resolves to; `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` moves the `capabilities: ['api.write']` action into a JSON block. The seat adopting this record adds the `security` label; the PR does not carry it now.

### ① Derived judgments

- Published surface: `@objectstack/skills` text only, nine files. No schema, no accept-set, no runtime path changes. Right.
- `packages/spec`: one script alias, one new script and one list file under `scripts/`, which the package's `files` array does not publish; one `NO_GENERATOR` ledger row. No published spec surface moves. Right, and the row's class is right: the check writes no artifact.
- New gate in a required lane (`typecheck-source-gates`, behind `TypeScript Type Check`): a rename, removal or duplicate of one of 24 headings, an undeclared JSON fence, or a JSON fence the spec refuses is now red for every contributor. That is the tightening the card orders. Right.
- The list against the hosted table: the 24 rows equal the 24 distinct `file` + `heading` pairs of `published-refs.ts` (9 data, 3 ui, 12 automation), and `item: 6` sits on the one row the table gives it. Right.
- Heading rule: `readSection` is the hosted `readPublishedSection` line for line (same `HEADING` regex, same fence toggle, same "next heading of the same or a higher level"), and the item test is the hosted `listItem` start regex. A verdict here is the verdict there. Right.
- Example coverage: two `os:check` TypeScript blocks left the type-check population (notify, the approval flow). Their JSON is held by `FlowNodeSchema` plus `flowNodeConfigRefusals`, and by `FlowSchema`, whose `superRefine` runs the same refusals per node (`flow.zod.ts` L1741). Not weaker than the type check it replaces. Right.
- Token ratchet: five rows raised, two lowered. Bytes re-read at both refs: 27988 to 28199, 5957 to 6170, 23652 to 23744, 26678 to 26859, 8974 to 9128, 16884 to 16811, 6985 to 6984; each row equals the ceiling of the priced bytes over four (7045, 1543, 5936, 6710, 2277, 4203, 1746). Ruling record 6513306068 letter B is quoted in each raised row and in the PR body, and each raised file shows deletions in the same file. Right. Two of the five paydowns (`objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`, `state-machines-and-approvals.md`) are syntax that left with the TypeScript block, not restatement; the ratchet's own rows carry the precedent "no same-file restatement was left to cut", and the gate is green on the head.
- Reading of ruling #34691 S3 = A ("a JSON form beside the TypeScript") and the card's scope line ("beside its TypeScript form, or a form neutral to both"): six sections now show JSON alone with a one-line TypeScript wrap note, not two blocks. Judged right: a JSON object literal is the TypeScript literal, each note names the wrapper (`ObjectSchema.create`, `defineFlow`, `definePermissionSet`, `defineAction`, `FlowNode`), and two copies of one shape would contradict the same ruling's "one copy of the shape knowledge". The dev did not flag it as a deviation; it is named here so the adopting seat sees the reading.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills: patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Matches what the diff publishes: wording and examples in shipped skill files, no behaviour. `packages/spec` needs no entry: nothing it publishes changed. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in both reports. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, carrier cloud: the check does not pin the two replaced passages. Answered: both occur exactly once in their sections at the head, byte for byte as the hosted table spells them (`type: 'schedule'` / `runAs: 'system'` in the time-relative flow; "a flow that must react to those too declares `runAs: 'system'`" in Approval Best Practices), and no diff line containing `runAs` is added or removed. The card's input list assigns that check to the cloud side. No action here.
- Dev flag, carrier cloud: five served sections now show JSON where the hosted pin shows TypeScript. Escalate to the cloud seat through objectstack-ai/cloud#4842: its tests on the delivered text are re-read when the pin moves past this PR. Not judged here.
- Dev flag, #35087 conflict in `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: the lane seat's sequencing; whichever lands second re-measures.
- Dev flag, node labels added in item 3: answered, `FlowNodeSchema.label` is a required string (`flow.zod.ts` L693).
- Dev flag (second report): `dispatch-gates --commands` did not derive the `check:generated` ledger reconcile for a diff that adds a `check:` script. Out of this PR's scope; the seat files it as a tooling follow-up or records why not.
- Deviations (interrupted gate run resumed, footer per AGENTS.md, first commits' trailers, 133 families not re-run on the one-row fix commit): the check-runs on the head answer the gate question; nothing for this record.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or in-app join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Per `hits` file:

- `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`: `notify` JSON keeps every key of the old block, and the four list items carry every old comment (required recipients and the `emailField` form, title XOR template, the RAW keys and defaults, the source pair and `actionUrl`). Item 3's two nodes match the old fragment plus the required `label`; the function registration stays TypeScript and says it has no JSON form. Holds.
- `references/examples-flows.md`: the TypeScript flow and its `runAs` line are untouched; the start node JSON equals the flow's start node; the window filter equals the old fragment with the 30 / 60 tiers moved to prose. Holds. See N3.
- `references/state-machines-and-approvals.md`: node for node and edge for edge the old flow; each `cel` tag is the envelope `cel()` returns (`expression.zod.ts` L490); the three comments are the three list items. Approver Types, Node Config and Approval Best Practices are untouched. Holds.
- `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: the object example follows the section's own rule (a team-shared business object is `public_read_write`) and authors every key the tables call for; the `expression` envelope is what `F` returns. Holds. See N1.
- `references/seeds.md`, `rules/naming.md`: one phrase each; item 6 of Critical Rules is untouched and still starts exactly one line. Holds.
- `rules/relationships.md`: the summary field keeps its three keys, and the optional two moved to prose with their meaning; the permission set shows the warned, masked and acknowledged cases the paragraph above it names, with the reason on a `readable: true` entry as the schema requires (`permission.zod.ts` L1039 to L1046). Holds.
- `rules/validation.md`: same rule, same seven states; `initialStates` and the terminal marker moved to one sentence. Holds.
- `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md`: the action carries `objectName`, a `locations` value the schema lists (`record_header`), and the same body and capability as the old inline fragment. Holds.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml`: one added step, nothing removed or reordered. It has an `id` and `continue-on-error: true`, which is the lane's contract: `lane-verdict.mjs` reads the roster from the workflow and each gate's `outcome`, so a red here fails the lane and a missing id would itself be red. No `if:`, no paths filter, so it runs on every trigger the workflow has (`push` to main, `pull_request`, `merge_group`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`). It cannot weaken an existing gate. It ran and passed on the head (step 27 of the lane).

Implementing files: the script agrees with its header and with the hosted reader sentence by sentence, apart from N2; the list file agrees with the hosted table; the ledger row and the ratchet rows agree with the tree.

Nits (none changes correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` drops "A custom object that omits it resolves to `private` at runtime, but the publish door rejects it before that". The ratchet row calls it a restatement of the `sharingModel` row; the refusal half is, the runtime half (ADR-0090 D1, the fail-closed default) is stated nowhere else in the published skills. What remains is correct and still orders the key authored on every object. Leave as an accepted deviation, or restore the clause in a later skills card.
- N2 (nit) — `check-skill-served-sections.ts` header says a JSON example cannot enter a served section unvalidated. A fence tagged `jsonc` or `json5`, or an untagged fence, is neither JSON nor TypeScript to `fencesOf` and passes in any form. Also nothing pins the list at 24 rows: a deleted row unpins its heading with the gate green (it is visible in the diff of a hand-kept file). Follow-up card, not this head.
- N3 (nit) — `examples-flows.md`: "As JSON the flow is that literal without `defineFlow(...)`" is loose, since the literal above carries comments and a placeholder `edges`. The start node that follows is exact.
- N4 (nit) — PR body: the `Verification` head still reads `84cede3db5`, and the body does not name the `check-generated.ts` row the fix commit added. The changeset says three neutral sections "drop a TypeScript-only phrase"; one of the three it means (seeds) labels the phrase rather than dropping it.

### Against the card

(2) A renamed, removed or duplicated pinned heading is red in `Type Check · source gates`, a required lane. The hosted half is objectstack-ai/cloud#4842. Nothing in the card is left for a later PR, so `Fixes` (not `Part of`) is right.

- **JSON alone in six sections, against "beside its TypeScript form".** I agree with the L2 reading: a JSON object literal is the TypeScript literal, and each section names its wrapper in one line. Two copies of one shape would go against the same ruling's "one copy".

### Read at the head

- **`check-skill-served-sections.ts`, read in full.**
  - `readSection` uses the same heading regex, fence toggle and same-or-higher-level end as the header says. The L2 compared it line for line with the hosted reader.

- **The gate ran on this head.** The CI log of job 134627624077 shows "self-test: 33 cases pass in 8 batteries" and "24 served section(s) … (6 json, 2 json+ts, 16 neutral); 10 JSON fence(s) parse and pass their spec validators". The step has an `id` and `continue-on-error: true` like its neighbours, so `Lane verdict` reads its outcome. The lane is `success`.
- **The skill hunks, read one by one.**
  - `notify`: every key and every old comment survive, as JSON plus a list.
  - Script plus `update_record`: same nodes, plus the `label` that `FlowNodeSchema` requires.
  - The approval flow: node for node and edge for edge the old one, and each `` cel`…` `` is now its `{ dialect, source }` envelope.
  - Summary field: same three keys, and the two optional keys moved to prose.
  - Permission set: the warned, masked and acknowledged cases, with the reason only on a `readable: true` entry.
  - State machine: same seven states.
  - Action: same body and `api.write` capability, now with a `locations` value.
  - No added or removed line contains `runAs`. The two passages the hosted door replaces are untouched.
- **Token ratchet, re-measured with `wc -c` at the head.** The rows are 7045, 1543, 5936, 6710, 2277, 4203 and 1746. Each equals ceil(bytes / 4), or ceil((bytes − 20) / 4) for the three `SKILL.md` files with a stamp line. Five rows go up and two go down, under ruling 6513306068 letter B, and each raised file also cuts lines.
- **Changeset.** This PR's own file. `@objectstack/skills: patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. No spec surface is published (the new files sit under `packages/spec/scripts/`, outside the `files` array). No `content/docs/releases/` path. No changeset already on main is edited.
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `aef42cba4e`. Main has not touched any of these paths since the base.

### Nits (none blocks)

- I agree with L2 N1: the runtime half of the deleted `sharingModel` clause ("resolves to `private`") is not restated anywhere else in the published skills.
- I agree with L2 N2: an untagged, `jsonc` or `json5` fence escapes the form check, and nothing pins the list at 24 rows. Both belong in a follow-up card.
- `examples-flows.md` drops "because the window is evaluated every day, a threshold is never missed". The spec still says it (`TIME_RELATIVE_DEFAULT_CRON` doc), and the cut is a token paydown, not a correction. It can be left out.
- The PR body's verification head still reads `84cede3d` (L2 N4), and the body has no attribution lines. The PR-body guards are green.
